mission_2.prediction: I predict the robot will reach the goal sooner with A* than with DFS on the constrained map. A* uses the distance traveled so far and the estimated distance to the goal to guide its search. DFS follows one branch at a time and can end up with a winding route. In Mission 1, A* found a 24.5 m route on the constrained map, while DFS found a 104 m route. The robot will have to slow down for turns around the walls, but with the same controller and speed limit, I expect A*’s shorter route to take less time to drive.
mission_2.performance: Yes. On the constrained map, A* succeeded in 90.19 simulated seconds after driving 23.91 m. DFS timed out after 180.44 simulated seconds and drove 44.08 m. At checkpoint 1760, the DFS trajectory ends near the bottom of the map, still 7.33 m from the goal. Its planned route was 104 m long, compared with 24.5 m for A*. That helps explain why DFS drove farther than A* and still ran out of time. The elapsed-time gap was larger on the open map, about 133 seconds versus 90 seconds on the constrained map. Both DFS times show when the trial stopped.
mission_2.choice: I would choose Nav2 Smac 2D because it completed both deliveries in the least driving time in my trials. It succeeded in 35.12 seconds on the open map and 73.75 seconds on the constrained map. A* also succeeded on both, but Nav2 drove 10.06 m versus A*’s 13.15 m on the open map, and 20.64 m versus 23.91 m on the constrained map. For a delivery, the advantage I care about most is reaching the destination sooner.
